Hi Evan — thanks for the clear ask and the matrix. Quick summary below and next steps. I'll loop in Rishi and Ben to confirm pricing mechanics.

Mixing tiers
- Contract model: we typically do a single master subscription with line-item allocations per team. Each line item can be a seat tier (developer seats) or a dedicated capacity allocation (Committed GPUs). Billing shows both a monthly amortized commit plus usage overages per line item.
- Example: 50 Developer seats (Tier A), 2 Dedicated pools (Medium / High). Each seat has a per-seat monthly rate; dedicated pools are committed throughput priced monthly.

Seat/feature swaps and credits
- Within first 90 days: we can provide prorated transfer credits when moving commitments between teams (same fiscal year).
- Between 90 and 270 days: swaps are supported but credits are reduced to 50% of prorated value to reflect provisioning costs.
- After 270 days: swaps are allowed but treated as forward reallocation (no cash refunds; seat credits only).
- For downgrades: we offer one-time downgrade credit equal to unused prepaid months for the downgraded component; this is capped at 25% of the annual commit for large deals (> $250k).

Feature bundling recommendation (based on your matrix)
- Core bundle (recommended for product line A): hosted API access, standard observability, 1 low-priority dedicated pool for burst.
- Enablement bundle (product lines B/C): private deployment options, increased retention for observability, priority support.

Proposed next steps
1) I'll ask Ben to produce a sample quote & seat-mix scenarios.
2) Rishi will confirm discount bands for the annual commit levels you might consider.
3) We will include the credit schedule in the MA.

I'll attach a template quote and a suggested MA draft by EOD today.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
